title: Babe Russin and shared Basie-Ellington tastes
summary: Tenor saxophonist Babe Russin was the first in the band to mention Lester Young and shared Leeman's love of Basie and Ellington over Dorsey's style.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: And he's still writing. And we had Babe Russin in that band, he's a great tenor saxophone player, and he was one of the first people that accepted Prez.
And he and I had something in Tommy Dorsey's band because I'm still oriented with Basie's band.
Now explain to me when you said he was one of the first people -- what was his name?
Okay, but what do you mean when you say he first accepted Prez?

He was the first -- well, I probably said that wrong, he was the first person that mentioned Prez, and when he found out that I knew about Basie's band, and Prez, I was surprised that anybody back east had heard of them.
I see, thank you for clarifying that.

And he didn't like the style of Tommy Dorsey's orchestra, because he was oriented the same way I was -- oriented, minded, in a Duke Ellington frame of mind or a Basie frame of mind, or a Fletcher Henderson, shall we say; whatever records we could grab.
